title: The Dodo Wasn't Dumb—It Might Have Been a Night Owl!
summary:
You've probably heard that dodos were dumb, clumsy birds that couldn't even run away from danger. But guess what? New research says that's totally wrong! Dodos might have actually been smart—and they might have loved the night.

Scientists used special scans to look inside dodo skulls and measure their brains. They found that dodo brains were the right size for their bodies, just like their pigeon cousins. So they weren't stupid at all. In fact, a 2016 study said dodos were probably as smart as modern pigeons, which can solve puzzles and understand ideas like space and time.

But here's the cool part: the part of the dodo's brain that helps with seeing was really small—similar to birds that are active at night. That means dodos probably didn't rely on their eyes much. 'The only situation where you're not relying on sight is when there is no light available,' said scientist Sara Citron. So dodos might have been nocturnal, meaning they slept during the day and were awake at night!

So why did everyone think dodos were dumb? Because when sailors came to their island, the dodos weren't afraid of humans. They would even run toward a dodo that was crying for help—which made it easy for sailors to catch them. But that's not because dodos were stupid. They lived on an island with no predators, so they never learned to be scared. It's like if you grew up in a house with no doors—you wouldn't know to lock them!

Dodos went extinct because humans brought animals like dogs and rats that ate their eggs. It wasn't their fault. So next time someone calls you a 'dodo,' tell them dodos were actually pretty cool—and maybe even party animals after dark!
why_it_matters: This matters because it shows that calling someone a 'dodo' as an insult is unfair, and that animals can be much smarter than old stories claim.

Article_Structure: WHO: Scientists like Sara Citron who study dodo skulls and brains.
WHAT: Found that dodos were smart and probably nocturnal, not dumb and clumsy as old stories claim.
WHERE: On the island where dodos lived before humans brought new predators like dogs and rats.
WHY: Dodos grew up without predators, so they were not afraid of humans; later, introduced animals ate their eggs and caused their extinction.

perspectives.description: They are happy that science is clearing the dodo's bad reputation and showing it was smart and adapted to its environment.
